# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

Only switch modes when the user explicitly asks you to or the current mode lacks a capability required to complete the request. Do not switch modes merely because the user asks a question.

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

70 |

19 |         r"\w{3} \d{1,2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}",  # Mon DD HH:MM:SS

1 | """Create an auditable, source-labelled catalogue from investigator output."""
2 | 
3 | from __future__ import annotations
4 | 
5 | import re
6 | 
7 | 
8 | _CITATION = re.compile(r"^(?P<file>.+?):(?P<line>\d+):\s*(?P<excerpt>.*)$")
9 | 
10 | 
11 | def build_evidence_catalog(investigators: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
12 |     """Return deterministic ``E-NNN`` facts without adding interpretation."""
13 |     facts: list[dict] = []
14 |     for investigator in investigators:
15 |         if investigator.get("status") != "complete":
16 |             continue
17 |         agent = investigator.get("agent", "Investigator")
18 |         for raw in investigator.get("evidence", []):
19 |             text = str(raw).strip()
20 |             if not text:
21 |                 continue
22 |             match = _CITATION.match(text)
23 |             source_file = match.group("file") if match else agent
24 |             line = int(match.group("line")) if match else None
25 |             excerpt = match.group("excerpt") if match else text
26 |             source_type = _source_type(agent)
27 |             facts.append({
28 |                 "id": f"E-{len(facts) + 1:03d}",
29 |                 "type": source_type,
30 |                 "attribution": "FACT",
31 |                 "investigator": agent,
32 |                 "source": source_file,
33 |                 "line": line,
34 |                 "excerpt": excerpt,
35 |                 "description": f"Extracted by {agent} from supplied evidence.",
36 |             })
37 |     return facts
38 |

13 | MAX_ZIP_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024
14 | MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES = 40 * 1024 * 1024

24 | def save_log(upload, destination: Path) -> str:
25 |     filename = secure_filename(upload.filename or "")
26 |     if not filename or Path(filename).suffix.lower() not in ALLOWED_LOG_EXTENSIONS:
27 |         raise ValueError("This file type is not supported. Logs must be .log or .txt files.")
28 |     if upload.content_length and upload.content_length > MAX_LOG_BYTES:
29 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded log is too large. The limit is 2 MB.")
30 |     target = destination / filename
31 |     upload.save(target)
32 |     if target.stat().st_size > MAX_LOG_BYTES:
33 |         target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
34 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded log is too large. The limit is 2 MB.")
35 |     return filename
36 | 
37 | 
38 | def _safe_member_path(root: Path, member_name: str) -> Path:
39 |     target = (root / member_name).resolve()
40 |     if root.resolve() not in target.parents and target != root.resolve():
41 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded ZIP contains an unsafe path.")
42 |     return target
43 | 
44 | 
45 | def save_project_zip(upload, destination: Path) -> str:
46 |     filename = secure_filename(upload.filename or "")
47 |     if not filename or Path(filename).suffix.lower() != ".zip":
48 |         raise ValueError("This file type is not supported. Project source must be a .zip file.")
49 |     if upload.content_length and upload.content_length > MAX_ZIP_BYTES:
50 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded ZIP is too large. The limit is 20 MB.")
51 |     archive_path = destination / filename
52 |     upload.save(archive_path)
53 |     if archive_path.stat().st_size > MAX_ZIP_BYTES:
54 |         archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
55 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded ZIP is too large. The limit is 20 MB.")
56 | 
57 |     extract_path = destination / "source"
58 |     extract_path.mkdir()
59 |     extracted_bytes = 0
60 |     try:
61 |         with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
62 |             for member in archive.infolist():
63 |                 if member.is_dir():
64 |                     continue
65 |                 target = _safe_member_path(extract_path, member.filename)
66 |                 extracted_bytes += member.file_size
67 |                 if extracted_bytes > MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES:
68 |                     raise ValueError("The uploaded ZIP expands beyond the 40 MB safety limit.")
69 |                 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
70 |                 with archive.open(member) as source, target.open("wb") as output:
71 |                     shutil.copyfileobj(source, output)
72 |     except (zipfile.BadZipFile, OSError, ValueError) as error:
73 |         shutil.rmtree(extract_path, ignore_errors=True)
74 |         if isinstance(error, ValueError):
75 |             raise
76 |         raise ValueError("The uploaded ZIP could not be processed safely.") from error
77 |     finally:
78 |         archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
79 |     return filename

69 |         self.events: list[TimelineEvent] = []

72 |         """Add an event to the timeline."""

75 |     def get_events_sorted(self) -> list[TimelineEvent]:
76 |         """Get events sorted by timestamp, with undated events at the end."""
77 |         dated = []
78 |         undated = []
79 | 
80 |         for event in self.events:
81 |             if event.timestamp:
82 |                 try:
83 |                     # Try to parse ISO format timestamp
84 |                     dated.append((datetime.fromisoformat(event.timestamp.replace('Z', '+00:00')), event))
85 |                 except (ValueError, AttributeError):
86 |                     undated.append(event)
87 |             else:
88 |                 undated.append(event)
89 | 
90 |         # Sort dated events by timestamp
91 |         dated.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
92 |         sorted_events = [event for _, event in dated] + undated
93 | 
94 |         return sorted_events
95 |

97 |         """Convert timeline to dictionary for JSON serialization."""
98 |         return {

21 |         Analyze available evidence and return readiness assessment.
22 |         
23 |         Returns dict with:
24 |         - score: 0-100 readiness percentage
25 |         - available: list of available evidence types
26 |         - missing: list of missing evidence types
27 |         - explanation: narrative description
28 |         """
29 |         available = []
30 |         missing = []
31 |         weight_sum = 0
32 |         available_weight = 0
33 |         
34 |         # Source code
35 |         if package.get("source_path"):
36 |             available.append("Source Code")
37 |             weight_sum += 25
38 |             available_weight += 25
39 |         else:
40 |             missing.append("Source Code (ZIP or GitHub repository)")
41 |             weight_sum += 25
42 |         
43 |         # Application logs
44 |         if package.get("logs_path"):
45 |             available.append("Application Logs")
46 |             weight_sum += 30
47 |             available_weight += 30
48 |         else:
49 |             missing.append("Application Logs from incident timeframe")
50 |             weight_sum += 30
51 |         
52 |         # Git history / Change evidence
53 |         if package.get("history_path"):
54 |             available.append("Git History & Changes")
55 |             weight_sum += 20
56 |             available_weight += 20
57 |         else:
58 |             missing.append("Git History (for commit analysis)")
59 |             weight_sum += 20
60 |         
61 |         # Stack trace / error report
62 |         observation = (package.get("user_observation") or "").lower()
63 |         has_stack_trace = any(token in observation for token in ["traceback", "stack trace", "exception", "at line"])
64 |         if has_stack_trace:
65 |             available.append("Stack Trace or Error Report")
66 |             weight_sum += 15
67 |             available_weight += 15
68 |         else:
69 |             missing.append("Stack Trace or detailed error report")
70 |             weight_sum += 15
71 |         
72 |         # Runtime evidence
73 |         has_runtime = any(token in observation for token in ["error", "failed", "timeout", "crash", "500"])
74 |         if has_runtime:
75 |             available.append("Runtime Error or Failure Evidence")
76 |             weight_sum += 10
77 |             available_weight += 10
78 |         else:
79 |             missing.append("Runtime reproduction or failure evidence")
80 |             weight_sum += 10
81 |         
82 |         score = int((available_weight / weight_sum * 100)) if weight_sum > 0 else 0
83 |         
84 |         return {
85 |             "readiness_score": score,
86 |             "available_evidence": available,
87 |             "missing_evidence": missing,
88 |             "readiness_level": _classify_readiness(score),
89 |             "explanation": _readiness_explanation(score, available, missing),

109 |         """
110 |         Analyze all investigators to determine overall evidence strength.
111 |         
112 |         Returns:
113 |         - strength_level: VERY_STRONG, STRONG, MODERATE, LIMITED, INSUFFICIENT
114 |         - percentage: 0-100 score
115 |         - sources_count: number of evidence sources analyzed
116 |         - breakdown: detail of each source's contribution
117 |         """
118 |         sources = []
119 |         strength_score = 0
120 |         max_score = 0
121 |         
122 |         for investigator in investigators:
123 |             agent = investigator.get("agent", "Unknown")
124 |             status = investigator.get("status", "unavailable")
125 |             confidence = investigator.get("confidence", 0.0)
126 |             findings = investigator.get("findings", [])
127 |             
128 |             if status == "complete":
129 |                 findings_count = len(findings)
130 |                 score = min(25, findings_count * 3) * confidence
131 |                 strength_score += score
132 |                 max_score += 25
133 |                 
134 |                 sources.append({
135 |                     "agent": agent,
136 |                     "status": "Available",
137 |                     "findings": findings_count,
138 |                     "confidence": f"{int(confidence * 100)}%",
139 |                 })
140 |             else:
141 |                 sources.append({
142 |                     "agent": agent,
143 |                     "status": "Unavailable",
144 |                     "findings": 0,
145 |                     "confidence": "0%",
146 |                 })
147 |                 max_score += 25
148 |         
149 |         percentage = int((strength_score / max_score * 100)) if max_score > 0 else 0
150 |         strength_level = _classify_strength(percentage)
151 |

"""
Unit tests for BugSleuth individual components.

Covers:
- models: Evidence, Hypothesis, IncidentTimeline / TimelineEvent, SimilarPattern, ProjectProfile
- services: evidence_catalog, trust_schema, timeline_builder, pattern_detector, investigation_summary
- utils: EvidenceBuilder
- services.file_service: save_log, save_project_zip, create_investigation_dir
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import zipfile
from io import BytesIO
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# models.Evidence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

from models.evidence import Evidence, EvidenceStrength, EvidenceType


class TestEvidenceModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Evidence:
        defaults = dict(
            evidence_id="EV-00001",
            investigator="Log Investigator",
            source_type=EvidenceType.APPLICATION_LOG,
            source_file="app.log",
        )
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Evidence(**defaults)

    def test_defaults_are_set(self):
        ev = self._make()
        assert ev.strength == EvidenceStrength.WEAK
        assert ev.tags == []
        assert ev.line_number is None
        assert ev.excerpt == ""

    def test_to_dict_contains_required_keys(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="ERROR request failed", line_number=42, tags=["error"])
        d = ev.to_dict()
        assert d["evidence_id"] == "EV-00001"
        assert d["source_type"] == "application_log"
        assert d["strength"] == "WEAK"
        assert d["line_number"] == 42
        assert d["tags"] == ["error"]

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="boom", strength=EvidenceStrength.STRONG, tags=["critical"])
        restored = Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict())
        assert restored.evidence_id == ev.evidence_id
        assert restored.strength == EvidenceStrength.STRONG
        assert restored.tags == ["critical"]

    def test_all_evidence_types_are_valid_enum_values(self):
        for ev_type in EvidenceType:
            ev = self._make(source_type=ev_type)
            assert ev.to_dict()["source_type"] == ev_type.value

    def test_all_strength_levels_round_trip(self):
        for strength in EvidenceStrength:
            ev = self._make(strength=strength)
            assert Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict()).strength == strength


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# models.Hypothesis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

from models.hypothesis import Hypothesis, HypothesisStatus


class TestHypothesisModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Hypothesis:
        defaults = dict(hypothesis_id="H-001", description="Falsy check caused failure")
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Hypothesis(**defaults)

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_below_zero(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=-5.0)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_above_one(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=99.0)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0

    def test_update_confidence_clamps(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.5)
        h.update_confidence(1.5)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0
        h.update_confidence(-0.1)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_add_supporting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        assert h.supporting_evidence.count("E-001") == 1

    def test_add_contradicting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        assert h.contradicting_evidence.count("E-002") == 1

    def test_set_status(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.set_status(HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED)
        assert h.status == HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED

    def test_to_dict_confidence_is_rounded(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.6666)
        assert h.to_dict()["confidence"] == 0.67

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.8, status=HypothesisStatus.LEADING)
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        restored = Hypothesis.from_dict(h.to_dict())
        assert restored.hypothesis_id == "H-001"
        assert restored.status == HypothesisStatus.LEADING
        assert "E-001" in restored.supporting_evidence


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# models.IncidentTimeline / TimelineEvent
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

from models.incident_timeline import IncidentTimeline, TimelineEvent, EventType


class TestIncidentTimeline:
    def _event(self, event_id: str, timestamp: str | None = None, event_type=EventType.ERROR) -> TimelineEvent:
        return TimelineEvent(
            event_id=event_id,
            event_type=event_type,
            description=f"Event {event_id}",
            timestamp=timestamp,
            source="test",
        )

    def test_add_and_count_events(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-001")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1"))
        tl.add_event(self._event("E2"))
        assert len(tl.events) == 2

    def test_get_events_sorted_by_timestamp(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-002")
        tl.add_event(self._event("late", "2026-08-29T12:00:00"))
        tl.add_event(self._event("early", "2026-08-29T08:00:00"))
        sorted_ids = [e.event_id for e in tl.get_events_sorted()]
        assert sorted_ids == ["early", "late"]

    def test_undated_events_appear_after_dated(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-003")
        tl.add_event(self._event("no-ts", timestamp=None))
        tl.add_event(self._event("dated", "2026-08-29T10:00:00"))
        sorted_ids = [e.event_id for e in tl.get_events_sorted()]
        assert sorted_ids.index("dated") < sorted_ids.index("no-ts")

    def test_to_dict_includes_event_count(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-004")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1"))
        d = tl.to_dict()
        assert d["event_count"] == 1
        assert d["investigation_id"] == "INV-004"

    def test_timeline_event_to_dict(self):
        ev = self._event("E99", "2026-01-01T00:00:00", EventType.DEPLOYMENT)
        d = ev.to_dict()
        assert d["event_type"] == "DEPLOYMENT"
        assert d["event_id"] == "E99"

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-005")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1", "2026-08-29T10:00:00", EventType.WARNING))
        restored = IncidentTimeline.from_dict(tl.to_dict())
        assert restored.investigation_id == "INV-005"
        assert len(restored.events) == 1
        assert restored.events[0].event_type == EventType.WARNING

    def test_empty_timeline_sorts_gracefully(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-006")
        assert tl.get_events_sorted() == []

class FakeUpload:
    """Minimal werkzeug FileStorage stand-in for unit testing."""

    def __init__(self, filename: str, data: bytes):
        self.filename = filename
        self._data = data
        self.content_length = len(data)
        self._buf = BytesIO(data)

    def save(self, dst: Path):
        dst.write_bytes(self._data)


class TestSaveLog:

class TestSaveProjectZip:
    def _make_zip(self, entries: dict[str, str]) -> bytes:
        buf = BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:

        return buf.getvalue()

from models.evidence import Evidence, EvidenceStrength, EvidenceType


class TestEvidenceModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Evidence:
        defaults = dict(
            evidence_id="EV-00001",
            investigator="Log Investigator",
            source_type=EvidenceType.APPLICATION_LOG,
            source_file="app.log",
        )
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Evidence(**defaults)

    def test_defaults_are_set(self):
        ev = self._make()
        assert ev.strength == EvidenceStrength.WEAK
        assert ev.tags == []
        assert ev.line_number is None
        assert ev.excerpt == ""

    def test_to_dict_contains_required_keys(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="ERROR request failed", line_number=42, tags=["error"])
        d = ev.to_dict()
        assert d["evidence_id"] == "EV-00001"
        assert d["source_type"] == "application_log"
        assert d["strength"] == "WEAK"
        assert d["line_number"] == 42
        assert d["tags"] == ["error"]

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="boom", strength=EvidenceStrength.STRONG, tags=["critical"])
        restored = Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict())
        assert restored.evidence_id == ev.evidence_id
        assert restored.strength == EvidenceStrength.STRONG
        assert restored.tags == ["critical"]

    def test_all_evidence_types_are_valid_enum_values(self):
        for ev_type in EvidenceType:
            ev = self._make(source_type=ev_type)
            assert ev.to_dict()["source_type"] == ev_type.value

    def test_all_strength_levels_round_trip(self):
        for strength in EvidenceStrength:
            ev = self._make(strength=strength)
            assert Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict()).strength == strength

from models.hypothesis import Hypothesis, HypothesisStatus


class TestHypothesisModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Hypothesis:
        defaults = dict(hypothesis_id="H-001", description="Falsy check caused failure")
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Hypothesis(**defaults)

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_below_zero(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=-5.0)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_above_one(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=99.0)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0

    def test_update_confidence_clamps(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.5)
        h.update_confidence(1.5)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0
        h.update_confidence(-0.1)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_add_supporting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        assert h.supporting_evidence.count("E-001") == 1

    def test_add_contradicting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        assert h.contradicting_evidence.count("E-002") == 1

        h.set_status(HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED)
        assert h.status == HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED

    def test_to_dict_confidence_is_rounded(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.6666)

from models.incident_timeline import IncidentTimeline, TimelineEvent, EventType


class TestIncidentTimeline:
    def _event(self, event_id: str, timestamp: str | None = None, event_type=EventType.ERROR) -> TimelineEvent:
        return TimelineEvent(
            event_id=event_id,
            event_type=event_type,
            description=f"Event {event_id}",
            timestamp=timestamp,
            source="test",
        )

    def test_add_and_count_events(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-001")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1"))
        tl.add_event(self._event("E2"))
        assert len(tl.events) == 2

    def test_get_events_sorted_by_timestamp(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-002")
        tl.add_event(self._event("late", "2026-08-29T12:00:00"))
        tl.add_event(self._event("early", "2026-08-29T08:00:00"))
        sorted_ids = [e.event_id for e in tl.get_events_sorted()]
        assert sorted_ids == ["early", "late"]

    def test_undated_events_appear_after_dated(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-003")
        tl.add_event(self._event("no-ts", timestamp=None))
        tl.add_event(self._event("dated", "2026-08-29T10:00:00"))
        sorted_ids = [e.event_id for e in tl.get_events_sorted()]
        assert sorted_ids.index("dated") < sorted_ids.index("no-ts")

    def test_to_dict_includes_event_count(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-004")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1"))
        d = tl.to_dict()
        assert d["event_count"] == 1
        assert d["investigation_id"] == "INV-004"

    def test_timeline_event_to_dict(self):
        ev = self._event("E99", "2026-01-01T00:00:00", EventType.DEPLOYMENT)
        d = ev.to_dict()
        assert d["event_type"] == "DEPLOYMENT"
        assert d["event_id"] == "E99"

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-005")
        tl.add_event(self._event("E1", "2026-08-29T10:00:00", EventType.WARNING))
        restored = IncidentTimeline.from_dict(tl.to_dict())
        assert restored.investigation_id == "INV-005"
        assert len(restored.events) == 1
        assert restored.events[0].event_type == EventType.WARNING

    def test_empty_timeline_sorts_gracefully(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-006")
        assert tl.get_events_sorted() == []

    def test_invalid_timestamp_treated_as_undated(self):
        tl = IncidentTimeline("INV-007")
        tl.add_event(self._event("bad-ts", "not-a-date"))
        tl.add_event(self._event("good-ts", "2026-01-01T00:00:00"))
        sorted_ids = [e.event_id for e in tl.get_events_sorted()]
        assert sorted_ids.index("good-ts") < sorted_ids.index("bad-ts")

class FakeUpload:
    """Minimal werkzeug FileStorage stand-in for unit testing."""

    def __init__(self, filename: str, data: bytes):
        self.filename = filename
        self._data = data
        self.content_length = len(data)
        self._buf = BytesIO(data)

    def save(self, dst: Path):
        dst.write_bytes(self._data)

class TestSaveProjectZip:
    def _make_zip(self, entries: dict[str, str]) -> bytes:
        buf = BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
            for name, content in entries.items():
                zf.writestr(name, content)
        return buf.getvalue()

    def test_saves_valid_zip(self, tmp_path):
        data = self._make_zip({"service.py": "x = 1"})

class FakeUpload:
    """Minimal werkzeug FileStorage stand-in for unit testing."""

    def __init__(self, filename: str, data: bytes):
        self.filename = filename
        self._data = data
        self.content_length = len(data)
        self._buf = BytesIO(data)

    def save(self, dst: Path):
        dst.write_bytes(self._data)

class TestSaveProjectZip:
    def _make_zip(self, entries: dict[str, str]) -> bytes:
        buf = BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
            for name, content in entries.items():
                zf.writestr(name, content)
        return buf.getvalue()

            save_project_zip(upload, tmp_path)

"""
Unit tests for BugSleuth individual components.

Covers:
- models: Evidence, Hypothesis, IncidentTimeline / TimelineEvent, SimilarPattern, ProjectProfile
- services: evidence_catalog, trust_schema, timeline_builder, pattern_detector, investigation_summary
- utils: EvidenceBuilder
- services.file_service: save_log, save_project_zip, create_investigation_dir
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import zipfile
from io import BytesIO
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# models.Evidence
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

from models.evidence import Evidence, EvidenceStrength, EvidenceType


class TestEvidenceModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Evidence:
        defaults = dict(
            evidence_id="EV-00001",
            investigator="Log Investigator",
            source_type=EvidenceType.APPLICATION_LOG,
            source_file="app.log",
        )
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Evidence(**defaults)

    def test_defaults_are_set(self):
        ev = self._make()
        assert ev.strength == EvidenceStrength.WEAK
        assert ev.tags == []
        assert ev.line_number is None
        assert ev.excerpt == ""

    def test_to_dict_contains_required_keys(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="ERROR request failed", line_number=42, tags=["error"])
        d = ev.to_dict()
        assert d["evidence_id"] == "EV-00001"
        assert d["source_type"] == "application_log"
        assert d["strength"] == "WEAK"
        assert d["line_number"] == 42
        assert d["tags"] == ["error"]

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        ev = self._make(excerpt="boom", strength=EvidenceStrength.STRONG, tags=["critical"])
        restored = Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict())
        assert restored.evidence_id == ev.evidence_id
        assert restored.strength == EvidenceStrength.STRONG
        assert restored.tags == ["critical"]

    def test_all_evidence_types_are_valid_enum_values(self):
        for ev_type in EvidenceType:
            ev = self._make(source_type=ev_type)
            assert ev.to_dict()["source_type"] == ev_type.value

    def test_all_strength_levels_round_trip(self):
        for strength in EvidenceStrength:
            ev = self._make(strength=strength)
            assert Evidence.from_dict(ev.to_dict()).strength == strength


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# models.Hypothesis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

from models.hypothesis import Hypothesis, HypothesisStatus


class TestHypothesisModel:
    def _make(self, **kwargs) -> Hypothesis:
        defaults = dict(hypothesis_id="H-001", description="Falsy check caused failure")
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return Hypothesis(**defaults)

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_below_zero(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=-5.0)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_confidence_is_clamped_above_one(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=99.0)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0

    def test_update_confidence_clamps(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.5)
        h.update_confidence(1.5)
        assert h.confidence == 1.0
        h.update_confidence(-0.1)
        assert h.confidence == 0.0

    def test_add_supporting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        h.add_supporting_evidence("E-001")
        assert h.supporting_evidence.count("E-001") == 1

    def test_add_contradicting_evidence_no_duplicates(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        h.add_contradicting_evidence("E-002")
        assert h.contradicting_evidence.count("E-002") == 1

    def test_set_status(self):
        h = self._make()
        h.set_status(HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED)
        assert h.status == HypothesisStatus.CONFIRMED

    def test_to_dict_confidence_is_rounded(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.6666)
        assert h.to_dict()["confidence"] == 0.67

    def test_round_trip_from_dict(self):
        h = self._make(confidence=0.8, status=HypothesisStatus.LEADING)

class TestPatternDetector:
    def test_returns_empty_for_none_path(self):
        assert PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(None) == []

    def test_returns_empty_for_nonexistent_path(self, tmp_path):
        assert PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path / "nope") == []

    def test_detects_falsy_value_validation(self, tmp_path):
        f = tmp_path / "service.py"
        f.write_text("if not payment_amount:\n    raise ValueError('bad')\n", encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "falsy_value_validation")
        assert len(patterns) >= 1
        assert patterns[0].risk_level.value == "MEDIUM"

    def test_detects_catch_all_exception(self, tmp_path):
        f = tmp_path / "handlers.py"
        f.write_text("try:\n    process()\nexcept:\n    pass\n", encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "catch_all_exception")
        assert len(patterns) >= 1

    def test_detects_silent_failure(self, tmp_path):
        f = tmp_path / "util.py"
        f.write_text("try:\n    risky()\nexcept:\n    pass\n", encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "silent_failure")
        assert len(patterns) >= 1
        assert patterns[0].risk_level.value == "HIGH"

    def test_max_results_is_respected(self, tmp_path):
        lines = "\n".join(f"if not x_{i}:" for i in range(20))
        (tmp_path / "big.py").write_text(lines, encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "falsy_value_validation", max_results=3)
        assert len(patterns) <= 3

    def test_unknown_pattern_type_returns_empty(self, tmp_path):
        (tmp_path / "a.py").write_text("x = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
        assert PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "nonexistent_pattern") == []

    def test_find_all_patterns_combines_types(self, tmp_path):
        (tmp_path / "mixed.py").write_text(
            "if not amount:\n    raise ValueError()\ntry:\n    go()\nexcept:\n    pass\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_all_patterns(tmp_path)
        types = {p.similarity_reason for p in patterns}
        assert len(types) >= 2

    def test_pattern_ids_are_unique(self, tmp_path):
        lines = "\n".join(f"if not v_{i}:" for i in range(5))
        (tmp_path / "f.py").write_text(lines, encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "falsy_value_validation")
        ids = [p.pattern_id for p in patterns]
        assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))

    def test_excerpt_is_truncated_to_150_chars(self, tmp_path):
        long_line = "if not " + "x" * 200 + ":"
        (tmp_path / "long.py").write_text(long_line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(tmp_path, "falsy_value_validation")
        assert all(len(p.excerpt) <= 150 for p in patterns)

    def test_single_file_path_is_accepted(self, tmp_path):
        f = tmp_path / "single.py"
        f.write_text("if not value:\n    pass\n", encoding="utf-8")
        patterns = PatternDetector.find_similar_patterns(f, "falsy_value_validation")
        assert len(patterns) >= 1

class FakeUpload:
    """Minimal werkzeug FileStorage stand-in for unit testing."""

    def __init__(self, filename: str, data: bytes):
        self.filename = filename
        self._data = data
        self.content_length = len(data)
        self._buf = BytesIO(data)

    def save(self, dst: Path):
        dst.write_bytes(self._data)
